name: Zion National Park
hook: Seven hours each way, which is exactly why nobody organises it and why it is worth organising.
whySeason: The best month there is. Highs in the mid-seventies, the cottonwoods along the Virgin River turning, and the summer crowds gone. The shuttle is still running, which matters more than it sounds.

drive.verdict: Drive. There is no scheduled service from Los Angeles that gets you to Springdale and back in a weekend, and once you are there the free shuttle does the canyon better than a car is allowed to.
drive.hoursNote: Kerb to kerb up the 15, before any stop.

fees.label: Park entrance
fees.note: Valid seven days. Splits across everyone in the car.

fees.label: Non-resident surcharge
fees.note: From 1 January 2026, every visitor aged 16 or over without US residency pays this on top of entry, at eleven parks. Zion is one. The $70 Zion annual pass does not waive it — that pass is for US citizens and residents. The $250 non-resident America the Beautiful pass does.

fees.label: Zion Canyon shuttle
fees.note: Free, no ticket, no reservation. Private cars are banned on the Scenic Drive throughout shuttle season, which covers both October weekends — so the car gets you to Utah and then stays parked.

itinerary.title: Watchman Trail at dusk
itinerary.what: After seven hours in a car you want the canyon to mean something before bed, and this is the one Zion hike that starts from the Visitor Center car park itself — no shuttle, no timing.3.3 miles round trip, about 480 feet of climb, roughly two hours on sandy uneven ground. It ends on a bench looking down the canyon at the Watchman with the lights of Springdale coming on below.
itinerary.catch: The trail is unlit, has drop-offs and steps up to 24 inches, and in early October the canyon walls take the light long before the sky goes dark. Start two hours before sunset, not one, or you finish the descent by phone torch on sandy rock.

itinerary.title: Angels Landing chains
itinerary.what: The reason to do this is not the summit photograph, it is the half mile before it: a ridge a few feet wide with what the park itself calls drop-offs of as much as 1,000 feet on each side, moving hand over hand along bolted chains. From The Grotto it is 1.9 miles and 1,187 feet to Scout Lookout, then the final half mile on the chains. Scout Lookout needs no permit at all and gets you the same view.
itinerary.cost: $6 per application, plus $3 per person if drawn
itinerary.catch: The seasonal lottery covering every date from 1 September to 30 November closed on 20 July 2026 — it is gone. All that is left is the day-before lottery, which shuts at 3pm Mountain Time the day before you hike, so you apply from the car on Friday and find out after you have already arrived. Plan the weekend so a no costs you nothing.

itinerary.title: The Narrows, bottom up
itinerary.what: You walk up the Virgin River itself between walls a thousand feet high and twenty feet apart. From the Temple of Sinawava the paved Riverside Walk runs a mile to where the path ends and the river becomes the trail. Go as far as Mystery Falls or push on to Wall Street — there is no summit, so you turn round when you have had enough.
itinerary.cost: Free from the bottom. No permit needed.
itinerary.catch: In October the water is cold enough that outfitters in Springdale hire drysuits, and the river is the trail — there is nowhere to go if a flash flood comes down. Check the park’s flash flood forecast the morning you go and do not argue with it.

itinerary.title: Canyon Overlook at sunrise
itinerary.what: A mile round trip for a view most people drive past. It sits just east of the Mount Carmel tunnel, which is one of the few stretches of the park you are still allowed to drive, so it works on the way out. Half an hour up, and the whole lower canyon opens underneath you.
itinerary.timeNeeded: 1 hour, plus the drive to the trailhead
itinerary.catch: The car park holds about a dozen cars and fills before dawn on an October weekend. The overflow is roadside on a blind bend in a tunnel approach, which is as bad an idea as it sounds.

name: San Francisco
hook: An hour and a half in the air, and the only Californian city that works better without a car than with one.
whySeason: The warmest, clearest month of the San Francisco year, which is the opposite of what visitors expect. The summer fog has gone and the city gets the fortnight of proper weather it spends the rest of the year denying it has.

drive.verdict: Do not drive. Six hours up the 5, then a car you pay to store and cannot use — the city is built for its own transit and the parking alone costs more than the flight saves.
drive.hoursNote: Kerb to kerb up the 5, before any stop.

fees.label: City entry
fees.note: Nothing to pay to be in the city. The costs here are the bed, getting there, and getting around.

transit.label: Fly LAX to SFO

fare.label: Return flight, LAX to SFO
fare.provider: Southwest, Alaska and United all fly it

local.label: BART from SFO, plus a Muni day pass
local.note: BART fares rose 6.2% in January 2026 and SFO carries a surcharge on top.

transit.hoursNote: 1h 25m in the air, plus the ride to LAX, two hours before departure, and BART into the city. The in-air figure is the small half of it.

parkingPerNight.label: Overnight parking
parkingPerNight.note: The line that decides the car question in San Francisco.

itinerary.title: The bridge by bike
itinerary.what: Hire a bike in the Marina, ride the bridge deck with the container ships going under you, and freewheel down into Sausalito for lunch. The ferry brings you and the bike back, which is the part that makes it a morning rather than a day.
itinerary.cost: Bike hire and the Sausalito ferry
itinerary.catch: The bridge is loud, cold and busier with pedestrians than the photographs suggest, and the west footway is closed to bikes at weekends. Ride early — by noon you are threading a crowd.

itinerary.title: Alcatraz
itinerary.what: The cell house audio tour is narrated by men who were imprisoned there and guards who worked there, and it is better than it has any right to be. The boat is part of it — the city recedes behind you exactly as it did for them.
itinerary.cost: Ferry and tour, from the official operator only
itinerary.catch: It sells out weeks ahead, and every same-day ticket you will be offered near the pier is a resale at a markup. If you have not booked before you fly, assume you are not going.

itinerary.title: The Mission, for dinner
itinerary.what: The best-value eating in the city and the reason to land on a Friday rather than a Saturday. A burrito the size of a forearm for under fifteen dollars, murals down Balmy Alley, and the 14 Mission or the J Church gets you there from anywhere downtown.
itinerary.catch: The bar scene here is the draw for a lot of people and all of it is 21 and over. Under 21 this is a food trip, and the food is genuinely the better half.

itinerary.title: Lands End
itinerary.what: A cliff path through cypress on the outer edge of the city, with the bridge appearing between the trees and the Sutro Baths ruins collapsing into the sea at the end of it. Almost nobody who visits San Francisco for a weekend does this, and it is the best hour the city has.
itinerary.timeNeeded: 2 hours including the 38 Geary out and back
itinerary.catch: This is the one corner of the city where the fog does not read the calendar. It can be clear downtown and completely socked in at Lands End, and the bridge you came to see will simply not be there.

name: Joshua Tree
hook: Two and a half hours out and the sky does something you will not have seen in Europe.
whySeason: The month the desert becomes survivable again. Highs in the mid-eighties instead of the hundred-and-tens of summer, nights cold enough for a jacket, and the clearest skies of the year.

drive.verdict: Drive, and there is no alternative worth pretending about. A coach reaches Palm Springs and a weekday bus reaches the town, but the park boundary is still five miles further and the good rock is fifteen beyond that, with no service inside and no signal to call anything.

fees.label: Park entrance
fees.note: Valid seven days, and it splits. Four people in one car pay $7.50 each.

fees.label: Non-resident surcharge
fees.note: Joshua Tree is not one of the eleven parks that levies the $100 surcharge. A foreign passport pays the standard rate here — which is why it is the cheapest weekend on this list by a distance.

itinerary.title: Hidden Valley loop
itinerary.what: A mile round a bowl of rock that cattle rustlers supposedly used as a natural corral, and the fastest way to understand what the park actually is. Boulders the size of houses, Joshua trees at every angle, and the loop is flat enough to do in trainers.
itinerary.catch: It is the first stop inside the west entrance, so it takes the full weight of the day-trip traffic from about ten in the morning. Get there before nine and you will have it nearly to yourself.

itinerary.title: Keys View at sunset
itinerary.what: A five-thousand-foot viewpoint looking straight down onto the San Andreas Fault, the Coachella Valley and the Salton Sea, with San Jacinto opposite. You drive to it, which for once is the point — the light goes orange across the whole valley floor and you are standing above it.
itinerary.catch: The wind at the top is genuinely cold after dark and there is no shelter. Also, the haze blowing in from Los Angeles can flatten the view entirely — a clear day in the park is not a clear view from Keys.

itinerary.title: The sky, after dark
itinerary.what: This is what you came for and it costs nothing. Joshua Tree is a Dark Sky Park within reach of Los Angeles, and on a moonless night the Milky Way is a solid band with structure in it. Pull off anywhere along Park Boulevard, turn the engine and the lights off, and give your eyes twenty minutes.
itinerary.timeNeeded: An hour, and you will stay longer
itinerary.catch: A bright moon washes the whole thing out, so check the phase before you settle on dates. And the desert drops twenty-five degrees after sunset; people arrive in shorts and leave after ten minutes.

itinerary.title: Jumbo Rocks scrambling
itinerary.what: No ropes, no skill, no guide. The granite here is coarse enough to walk up at angles that look impossible, and Skull Rock is at the roadside for the photograph. It is the most fun you can have in the park without equipment.
itinerary.catch: Coarse granite takes skin off, going down is much harder than going up, and there is no phone signal to call anybody if you misjudge it. Stay within what you can reverse.

name: San Diego
hook: The Surfliner runs along the sand for the last hour, and you never need a car once you arrive.
whySeason: Locals call it the second summer. The marine layer that greys out May and June is long gone, the water is at its warmest of the year, and the crowds went home in August.

drive.time: 2h 15m each way, worse on a Friday
drive.verdict: A car here is money spent on a problem. The train goes along the coast for the last hour, the trolley and the MTS buses reach the beaches and Balboa Park, and Balboa introduced paid parking in January 2026 — so driving buys you a queue on the I-5 and somewhere to pay overnight.
drive.hoursNote: Kerb to kerb on the 5, and reliably worse leaving LA on a Friday afternoon.

fees.label: City entry
fees.note: Nothing to pay to be there. Balboa Park is free to walk through; the museums inside it are not.

transit.label: Amtrak Pacific Surfliner

fare.label: Return fare, LA Union Station to San Diego
fare.note: Students aged 25 and under get 15% off the adult fare, already applied here.

transit.hoursNote: 2h 45m on the train, plus about 30 minutes to Union Station and the walk off at the far end.

parkingPerNight.label: Overnight parking
parkingPerNight.note: Balboa Park added paid parking in January 2026, so a car costs you at both ends.

itinerary.title: La Jolla Cove
itinerary.what: Sea lions and harbour seals hauled out on the rocks at eye level, close enough that the smell is part of the experience. The cliff path above the cove runs a mile with the animals below you the whole way, and the water in the cove itself is the clearest in Southern California.
itinerary.catch: They are wild animals on a public beach and people get far too close for a photograph. There is a legally enforced distance, the bulls do charge, and the pupping-season closures move without much notice.

itinerary.title: Balboa Park
itinerary.what: Fourteen hundred acres of Spanish Colonial Revival built for a 1915 exposition and never taken down, with seventeen museums inside it. Walking the grounds, the Botanical Building and the lily pond costs nothing, and that alone is worth the afternoon.
itinerary.catch: Paid parking arrived in January 2026, so arriving by car now costs you before you start — take the 7 bus. And seventeen museums is a trap: pick two, or you will spend the day queueing rather than looking.

itinerary.title: Sunset Cliffs
itinerary.what: A mile of eroding sandstone bluff on the western edge of Point Loma, facing directly into the sunset with nothing between you and Hawaii. It is where the city goes to watch the day end, and it is free.
itinerary.catch: The cliffs are actively crumbling and the fenced-off sections are fenced off for a reason — people fall from here every year, usually while stepping back for a photograph.

itinerary.title: The Gaslamp, or not
itinerary.what: Sixteen blocks of Victorian commercial buildings turned into the city’s going-out district, and the default answer to what to do on a Saturday night in San Diego.
itinerary.cost: Free to walk; everything inside is not
itinerary.catch: After dark this is effectively a 21-and-over district — the bars card at the door and most of the venues will not admit you at all under 21. If that is the group, Little Italy two blocks north is restaurants rather than bars and stays open to everyone.
